definitions.explanation: A soft, soupy dish made by cooking rice in a large amount of water until it becomes very soft. Commonly eaten when sick or for gentle nourishment.

examples.japanese: {風邪|かぜ}のときはお{粥|かゆ}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: When I have a cold, I eat rice porridge.

examples.japanese: {梅干|うめぼ}しを{入|い}れたお{粥|かゆ}がおいしい。
examples.english: Rice porridge with pickled plum is delicious.

examples.japanese: {七草|ななくさ}{粥|がゆ}を{食|た}べて{無病息災|むびょうそくさい}を{願|ねが}う。
examples.english: We eat seven-herb porridge and pray for good health.

notes:
Usually used with the polite prefix お as お{粥|かゆ}. Also read as かい in some compounds.

TYPES:
- お{粥|かゆ}: plain rice porridge
- {七草|ななくさ}{粥|がゆ}: seven-herb porridge (eaten January 7)
- {茶|ちゃ}{粥|がゆ}: tea porridge (Nara/Wakayama specialty)
- {卵|たまご}{粥|がゆ}: egg porridge

CULTURE: Eating {七草|ななくさ}{粥|がゆ} on January 7th ({人日|じんじつ}の{節句|せっく}) is a long-standing Japanese tradition. The seven spring herbs are believed to promote good health and give the stomach a rest after the rich New Year's food.

NUANCE: お{粥|かゆ} is strongly associated with being ill in Japan. Offering to make someone お{粥|かゆ} is a caring gesture, similar to making chicken soup in Western cultures.
